title: Connected Confidence Intervals under Rare Outcome Adjudication with Poisson False-Positive Counts
banked_reason: D0.5 typed triage: delivered incremental tier below field floor; not salvageable in scope. Four panel findings remain unrepaired, so mathematical soundness of the note and numerical certificate is not established.
gap_reasons: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation constructed a Gaussian-Poisson count-indexed connected-interval value and a finite-trial expanding-local bracket with an attainable count-blind upper endpoint. A uniform center-free finite-data procedure attaining the smaller count-using value remained open; D0.5 therefore graded the delivered contribution incremental, below the field floor. The numerical certificate and convergence conditions also retain unrepaired soundness findings, so this bank entry records research artifacts and a terminal tier decision, not a verified theorem.
tldr: Along a prespecified triangular decision boundary, or an externally calibrated deployment sequence, both the review probability and the one-sided false-positive probability scale as \(n^{-1/2}\); this is not asserted to be a generic practical-trial regime. Reported-risk noise is Gaussian while discovered false positives remain Poisson. The paper proves the count-indexed connected-action value and its zero-axis-safe outward-rounded computation. For the finite trial it proves \(V_{c,T,\alpha}(r)\le\lim_H\liminf_n L_n(r,H)\le\lim_H\limsup_n L_n(r,H)\le V^{\mathrm{cb}}_{T,\alpha}(r)\), with the count-blind endpoint attained by globally honest \(r\)-indexed procedures. At the certified point the bracket is \(3.7989619796\) to less than \(4.2214\). The Hoeffding interval supplies an exact all-row fallback, while one center-free sequence attaining the smaller count-using value remains open.
gap: Regular two-phase causal estimators rely on a Gaussian validation contribution, whereas generic minimax confidence-set theory does not resolve connected actions, unrestricted location, finite Poisson counts, and unknown experiment parameters together.
